# Proposal

I plan to investigate how weather, seasonality, and building/location characteristics drive electricity consumption and cost across NYC public buildings over the past 15 years. My motivation is twofold: electricity is one of the largest controllable operating expenses for large building portfolios, and understanding what most strongly explains consumption variation has direct implications for budgeting, sustainability planning, and the city's decarbonization goals. I will combine two data sources of different types: (1) NYC Open Data's Electric Consumption And Cost (2010 – Sep 2025) dataset, pulled via the Socrata API, which provides monthly kWh usage and charges by account, borough, and building development; and (2) historical NYC weather data (daily temperatures and heating/cooling degree days) retrieved from the NOAA / Open-Meteo API, which I'll aggregate to monthly and join on date to test how temperature drives consumption. The workflow will follow a standard acquire → tidy → transform → analyze → present pattern in R/RMarkdown: reshaping billing periods to a clean monthly long format, parsing dates, joining the weather data, then producing descriptive visualizations (time series by borough, consumption-vs-temperature scatter plots) and at least one statistical model (a regression of monthly consumption on cooling/heating degree days and borough). As a feature beyond what we covered in class, I'm planning to use either time series decomposition (stl/forecast) or an interactive leaflet map of average consumption by location. I'll work solo, and deliver everything via GitHub.

Data source: https://data.cityofnewyork.us/Housing-Development/Electric-Consumption-And-Cost-2010-Sep-2025-/jr24-e7cr/about_data
